title: Explicit block-encodings for biharmonic boundary-value problems
abstract: The biharmonic equation is a prototypical fourth-order partial differential equation whose high-dimensional discretization suffers from rapidly growing degrees of freedom and severe ill-conditioning. We develop QSVT--VTAA quantum linear-system algorithms by constructing explicit block-encodings tailored to periodic, simply supported, and Dirichlet--Neumann boundary conditions. For periodic and simply supported problems, Fourier and sine-transform diagonalizations yield augmented Poisson systems with the condition-number scaling of a second-order operator. For Dirichlet--Neumann problems, we introduce a second-order boundary-corrected finite-difference discretization, establish mesh-independent stability, and construct an explicit block-encoding of the resulting nonsymmetric matrix. We also formulate a coupled-Laplace system with additional boundary unknowns and characterize its complexity in terms of the condition number of the complete augmented matrix. The analysis covers discretization error, block-encoding normalization, gate complexity, and solution extraction under an amplitude-input and quantum-state-output model. Numerical experiments validate the proposed discretizations and the corresponding linear solves.
summary: This paper presents a theoretical framework to solve biharmonic boundary-value problems using advanced quantum linear algebra techniques. By constructing explicit block-encodings for the discretized operators, the authors apply QSVT-VTAA algorithms to achieve efficient solutions across various physical boundary conditions. This work advances the application of quantum computation to classical computational physics challenges.
main_problem: Developing quantum linear-system algorithms for solving high-order partial differential equations, specifically the biharmonic boundary-value problem.
main_result: The authors developed explicit block-encodings tailored to various boundary conditions (periodic, simply supported, Dirichlet–Neumann) and demonstrated that QSVT-VTAA can solve these systems with condition number scaling improvements over direct methods.
method: The core method involves constructing explicit block-encodings of the discretized differential operators and applying Quantum Singular Value Transformation combined with Variable Time Amplitude Amplification (QSVT-VTAA).
model_or_system: The model is the biharmonic equation ($\Delta^2 u = f$), which arises in continuum mechanics. The problem is discretized using finite-difference or spectral methods, leading to large, sparse linear systems $Ax=b$.
key_observables: Condition number scaling ($\kappa(A)$), gate complexity, discretization error ($L^2$ and $L^\infty$ norms), and solution extraction cost.
important_parameters: The order of the PDE (fourth-order), boundary conditions (periodic, simply supported, Dirichlet–Neumann), and system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: Assumes that normalized quantum states for the right-hand side and boundary data are efficiently preparable; separates discretization errors from quantum state-preparation errors.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic circuits for LCU construction, basic QSVT diagrams, and visualizations of boundary reflections used in Laplacian block-encodings.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the challenge of high-order PDEs. It then details the quantum algorithmic framework (QSVT-VTAA) and how to construct necessary block-encodings for specific boundary conditions, culminating in numerical validation across different physical scenarios.
why_interesting: While focused on PDE solving rather than direct AMO Hamiltonians, the techniques developed—especially efficient block-encoding of structured operators and leveraging QSVT for large sparse matrices—are foundational tools applicable to simulating quantum many-body systems governed by differential equations or complex lattice models.
